summary: Josephine County, OR ground site on Whiskey Peak, Rogue River NF; L-4 cab (1930) salvaged in 1989 for the Sand Mountain Lookout; foundation reported still on the summit in 2019.

facts.design: Ground-mounted gable-roof L-4 cab, grange-hall style (1930 replacement)
facts.status_note: Cab salvaged in 1989 and rebuilt as the Sand Mountain Lookout near Sisters; a 2019 field-trip guide says the old foundation still remains on the summit

staffing.status: Forest Service lookouts 1929 to 1936; Aircraft Warning Service observers 1942 to 1943; no later staffing in the sources read

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Rogue River National Forest

access.note: Forest Service lists Whisky Peak Trail #910, and a 2019 public field trip reached the summit; no closures or current conditions found in the sources read

visit.drive_up: Forest Service roads, mostly in good shape, high clearance recommended; limited trailhead parking (2019 field-trip guide)
visit.trail_note: Short, steep trail to the summit, Whisky Peak Trail #910; no lookout structure to climb

events.note: Small frame cabin on the summit (FFLOS, firelookout.com); Oregon Lookouts quotes a Rogue River NF history dating the lookout house to 1924
Lookout house destroyed by fire in October 1929; lookout Cal Winningham lost his belongings
Replacement ground-mounted gable-roof L-4 cab completed in October 1930 with a concrete floor
Mr. and Mrs. George Ellis in charge of the lookout for the summer
Aircraft Warning Service post activated August 26, 1942; FFLOS says an AWS cabin was built here in 1942
Aircraft Warning Service post deactivated October 16, 1943; Forest Service retained the structures for fire spotting
Cab salvaged, bundled and flown out by helicopter for the Sand Mountain Lookout near Sisters
Registered April 22, 2011 as US 935, OR 293; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says an AWS cabin was built in 1942; the 1944 AWS report quoted by Oregon Lookouts says the service used existing Forest Service facilities and added sleeping quarters. The story follows the report.

The register, firelookout.com and Oregon Lookouts use Whiskey Peak; the Sand Mountain Society, the field-trip guide and the Forest Service trail use Whisky Peak. The story uses Whiskey for the site and notes the other spelling where a source uses it.

notes_for_editor: The 1989 salvage and the 2011 register entry are well sourced. Unresolved: the first house date (1922 register and firelookout.com vs 1924 Rogue River NF history via Oregon Lookouts); the builder (Forest Service per the register and Oregon Lookouts vs CCC per the 2019 field-trip guide); and the trail length (field-trip guide says half-mile; a Forest Service search snippet says 0.8 miles, not read in full, so not cited). Foundation remains rest on one 2019 guide only; Applegate Siskiyou Alliance Facebook snippets also mention a foundation and an outhouse but were seen only in search results, so they are not cited. The access level 'public' is an inference from the Forest Service trail and a 2019 public field trip; check closures. The Forest Service trail page was read but its cached text has only the heading. Used 1 WebSearch call and 6 page reads. Oregon Lookouts marks the site 'Removed' at the end of its entry; the brief's record matches the sources; no corrections.
